title: The largest exempt holdings
question: Where is the exempt value? The largest institutional holdings on the 2025 roll, by address.
finding: Ten addresses hold $5.26 billion of the $16.04 billion exempted, 33% of it. The largest are 1101 Van Ness Avenue (hospitals, welfare exemption, $2.67 billion); 3555 Cesar Chavez Street (hospitals, welfare exemption, $693.8 million); 151 3rd Street (commercial/mixed use, welfare exemption, $309.3 million); 2130 Fulton Street (schools, college/university, church exemption, $293.6 million). By the roll’s own description of use, the exempt value sits mostly in hospitals ($4.60 billion); apartment 15 units or more ($3.48 billion); schools ($1.72 billion); office ($1.37 billion).
how: Parcels on the 2025 roll with an institutional exemption code, grouped by the street address the roll prints and ranked by exempt value. Use is the roll’s property class. The tax column applies the 1% basic rate. Parcels the roll classes as single-family homes, flats, condominiums or small apartment buildings are counted in the totals but left out of this list.
limits: Hospitals, universities and nonprofit housing are exactly what these exemptions are for, and a large holding is a large institution, nothing more. The roll does not name the owner; the address identifies the building, and anyone can match it to an institution, but this list does not. A parcel can be partly exempt, which is why exempt value and assessed value differ. What would turn this into a test: the claim file for each parcel, showing who claimed and for what use.

sources.t: San Francisco Assessor-Recorder: Secured Property Tax Rolls, roll years 2019, 2022 and 2025 (DataSF)
